BiblicalUsage: Abel-mizraim — the mourning of the Egyptians — is named once, in Genesis 50:11, when the Canaanites watch Joseph's funeral procession for Jacob: 'This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians: wherefore the name of it was called Abel-mizraim, which is beyond Jordan.' It is the threshing floor of Atad, renamed by seven days of lament.
TheologicalSignificance: A place gets its name from grief — the Egyptians mourned Jacob for seven days, and the Canaanites could not miss it. I believe Abel-mizraim says something true about mourning: it is public, it is long, and it honours the dead in a way strangers can see.
